preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= 50000 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for x in line.split())
preconditions.description: n (number of tournaments) satisfies 1 ≤ n ≤ 50000, and k (number of sports) satisfies 1 ≤ k ≤ 10.
The input has exactly n + 1 lines: first line contains n and k, followed by n lines of sportsman data.

preconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == k for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each of the n lines after the first contains exactly k integers representing the sportsman's power in each sport.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(sij) <= 10**9 for i in range(1, n + 1) for sij in stdin.splitlines()[i].split())
preconditions.description: Each power sij (1 ≤ sij ≤ 10^9) is a positive integer.

preconditions.expression: all(any(int(sij) != int(sik) for j in range(k) for ik in range(j + 1, k)) for i in range(1, n + 1) for sij in stdin.splitlines()[i].split())
preconditions.description: For each sportsman, all powers in the k sports are distinct.

postconditions.expression: stdout == '\n'.join(str(count_possible_winners(i, k, sportsmen)) for i in range(1, n + 1)) + '\n'
postconditions.description: For each tournament year i (1 ≤ i ≤ n), the output line contains the number of possible winners in the i-th tournament, where sportsmen are the first i participants.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(count) <= i for i, count in enumerate(stdout.splitlines(), 1))
postconditions.description: The count of possible winners for the i-th tournament is between 1 and i (inclusive), as at least one sportsman (the last one) can always win, and no more than i sportsmen can be possible winners.
